code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: SAA cell longitudes are direct outputs of WMM-2025 / CHAOS-7 / IGRF-13, derived from geodynamo MHD of reversed-flux patches at the core-mantle boundary (Terra-Nova & Amit 2017 PEPI 266:39-53). Dome adopts the same numerical position while relabeling the mechanism as aetheric field decay.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: SAA western cell has been documented west of 45°W since the early 20th century; the modern two-cell morphology is well-established in WMM/CHAOS-7 outputs. W022 registered 2026-03-12, decades after the observation was public. No timestamped pre-registration of the specific 45°W threshold in an independent venue was found this cycle either.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: H(r) = 8537·exp(-r/8619) has zero azimuthal derivative. FSF = H(r)/r inherits the same axial symmetry. No dome equation (H(r), FSF, or the WIN-053-quoted B(r) = A·e^(-r_N/λ) + C·e^(-r_S/λ)) contains a longitude term; all depend only on polar-radial distance. 45°W is a fixed number adopted from WMM/CHAOS output, not derived.

holes_found.description: The axial-symmetry argument attacks H(r) (firmament-height function) but the dome-side equation most directly relevant to geomagnetic predictions is FSF = H(r)/r (raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 22) or B(r) = A·e^(-r_N/λ) + C·e^(-r_S/λ) (per WIN-053 quotation). A dome defender could correctly respond: 'H(r) is firmament height, not our field equation — you are attacking the wrong term. Our field-strength factor is FSF, and our field equation is B(r).' The rebuttal is defeatable because FSF = H(r)/r also has zero azimuthal derivative and B(r) is axially symmetric (depends only on r_N and r_S, both polar-radial). But the current text does not preempt the semantic move. A reader who accepts the swap on face value walks away thinking we attacked the wrong equation.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a parenthetical after the first mention of H(r): '...H(r) = 8537·exp(−r/8619) (and the derived field-strength factor FSF = H(r)/r used for the dome's other geomagnetic predictions, per raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 22) depends only on radial distance r from the Axis Mundi and has zero azimuthal derivative...'. Optionally, one more clause: '...as does the dome's field equation B(r) = A·e^(−r_N/λ) + C·e^(−r_S/λ) referenced in WIN-053, which likewise carries no longitude term.' Preempts the semantic-swap defense and unifies terminology with WIN-053.

holes_found.description: Ambiguity between centre and boundary interpretation of 'West of 45 deg W'. Raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 62 says 'SAA western cell position: West of 45 deg W'. The word 'position' is not disambiguated — centroid or eastern boundary of the western cell. Our current text interprets as centroid (65-75°W) and derives the 20-30° gap accordingly. Under a boundary interpretation the eastern edge of the American SAA cell in modern models sits at roughly 15-30°W, which trivially satisfies 'west of 45°W' with an even larger safety margin. Argument holds under both readings; but a defender could claim we constructed our 20-30° gap from an unfavourable interpretation. Not load-bearing but worth acknowledging in one clause.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a one-clause hedge after the 20-30° figure: '...whether West of 45°W is read as centroid position (currently ~65-75°W, gap ~20-30°) or as the western cell's eastern boundary (currently ~15-30°W, gap already zero or negative), the >100-year falsifiability horizon holds under both readings.' Costs ~180 characters and closes a defender opening.

holes_found.description: Cross-WIN terminology divergence with WIN-053 remains unresolved. WIN-053 uses B(r) = A·e^(-r_N/λ) + C·e^(-r_S/λ) as the dome geomagnetic equation for the toroidal-topology argument. WIN-040 uses H(r) = 8537·exp(-r/8619) for the same axial-symmetry point (verified afresh via grep: WIN-053 has 9 mentions of B(r), 2 of H(r), 0 of FSF). Both arguments are correct and both support the axial-symmetry-implies-no-longitude-structure conclusion, but the different equation names invite a reader (or defender) to ask 'which is the actual dome field equation?' c4 flagged this and recommended a cross-WIN unifying pass; that pass has not shipped. Low urgency because the arguments are internally coherent; still worth logging as a known consistency debt.
holes_found.recommendation: Roll into a single cross-WIN terminology pass covering WIN-040, WIN-053, and any other WIN that invokes axial symmetry. Recommend a standardized frame: (a) H(r) = firmament-height, (b) FSF = H(r)/r used for magnetometer predictions, (c) B(r) = A·e^(-r_N/λ) + C·e^(-r_S/λ) quoted in the WIN-053 detail as the dome's geomagnetic field equation, (d) all three are axially symmetric so no dome equation carries a longitude term. Non-blocking; can bundle into the next holistic terminology-consistency pass.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model is correct that no derivation from first principles predicts a specific SAA western-cell longitude — even the standard geodynamo cannot pre-register 1900-vintage SAA positions without input data (data/wins.json WIN-040 detail_evidence acknowledges this at the sentence 'Standard MHD does not pre-register a specific 1900-vintage SAA longitude either'). The dome's post-hoc adoption is structurally similar to how the standard model would present the same value if asked. This is a real epistemic parity point (data/wins.json:WIN-040.detail_evidence).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The parity dissolves under the derivation-path test that Part 3.1b applies (see funwithscience.net/dome-model-review/#posthoc-standard, hyperlinked from WIN-040 detail_verdict_text): standard MHD derives the two-cell morphology, westward-drift dynamics, and current positions from first-principles core-dynamo behaviour over reversed-flux patches (Terra-Nova & Amit 2017 PEPI 266:39-53, DOI 10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002, cited in data/wins.json:WIN-040.detail_evidence) — a derivation the dome does not have and structurally cannot have because H(r), FSF = H(r)/r, and the WIN-053-quoted B(r) all lack any longitude term (raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 22 for FSF; data/wins.json:WIN-053.detail_evidence for B(r)). The dome adopts the WMM/CHAOS-7 end state; the standard model derives it. That is not the same epistemic move even though the numerical output matches.

advocate_mode.best_defense: You attack the wrong equation. H(r) is our firmament-height function — it describes the geometric shape of the dome, not the magnetic field. Our field-strength factor is FSF = H(r)/r (documented in raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 22) and our geomagnetic field equation is B(r) = A·e^(−r_N/λ) + C·e^(−r_S/λ) (see WIN-053's own quotation of our text). You have taken a geometry equation, noted its axial symmetry, and pretended that proves our field predictions cannot be longitude-specific. That is a category error — a rigorous reviewer would attack FSF or B(r), not H(r). Additionally: 'West of 45°W' in W022 refers to the western cell's eastern boundary, not its centroid, so your ~20-30° gap arithmetic is built from a misreading of our own prediction.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: One-line surgical patch to detail_evidence: after 'H(r) = 8537·exp(−r/8619)' add the parenthetical '(and the derived field-strength factor FSF = H(r)/r used for the dome's magnetometer predictions per raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 22, which inherits the same axial symmetry)'. Additionally, a ~180-character hedge that acknowledges the centre-vs-boundary ambiguity while showing the >100-year horizon holds under either reading. Both patches are surgical; no verdict change; no analytical rewrite; can be routed as a single decider self-apply.
